treaty_name: Convention between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Sudan for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and capital (1975)
eif_quote: The tax convention entered into force on 8 October 1977. It is effective in Sudan from 1 January 1975 and in the UK from: 1 April 1975 for Corporation Tax; 6 April 1975 for Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax
source_title: gov.uk: UK–Sudan Income and Capital Tax Convention 1975 (in force)

rates.quote: Such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State but where the recipient is the beneficial owner of the dividend the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

but where such interest is derived by a resident of the other Contracting State who is subject to tax there in respect thereof the tax so charged in the Contracting State in which the interest arises shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

but where such royalties are derived by a resident of the other Contracting State who is subject to tax there in respect thereof the tax so charged in the Contracting State in which the royalties arise shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.basis: none (Sudan is not an MLI signatory; treaty has no general PPT)
ppt.quote: (8) The provisions of this Article shall not apply if the debt-claim in respect of which the interest is paid was created or assigned mainly for the purpose of taking advantage of this Article and not for bona fide commercial reasons.

notes: Effective dates (Art. 29): Sudan from 1 Jan 1975; UK from 6 Apr 1975 (income tax) and 1 Apr 1975 (corporation tax); valid_from set to 1975-01-01. Art. 10(3): Sudan-source dividends are exempt in Sudan so long as Sudan exempts dividends paid to non-residents (conditional, not modelled). Art. 10(4): UK tax-credit regime (tax at no more than 15% on dividend plus credit, else exempt) applies only so long as UK individuals get a dividend tax credit; that credit was abolished from April 2016, so the 15% cap of Art. 10(2) governs. Art. 10(6): the limits do not apply to dividends paid out of profits earned before a 10%+ holding was acquired, unless bona fide. Interest and royalty caps require the recipient to be subject to tax in its residence State. Anti-abuse rule for interest only (Art. 11(8)). The UK lists this treaty under the MLI, but Sudan is not an MLI signatory, so the MLI does not apply.
